close_reason: Defensive bead, no action required. The typed-Id / typed-State parameter pattern across the method API is correct and intentional, established by the JMAP-6by7.2 refactor. The bead documents the reasoning to defend against a future contributor proposing 'let's accept &str because it's simpler'. The in-tree comment trail (e.g. email.rs:340-342 noting which tests became impossible to express under typed Id and were deleted) already captures this. Nothing to add; nothing to remove. Closing as 'documented in-tree, no code action needed'.
description:
Every method signature uses `&Id`, `&[Id]`, `Option<&[Id]>` for id-shaped
parameters and `&State` for state tokens, rather than `&str` / `&[&str]`.
The typed API at the call site eliminates an entire class of bug that the
pre-typed shape was vulnerable to (empty-id strings, malformed Ids, state
tokens swapped with arbitrary strings).

A contributor who has not internalized this might propose "let's accept
`&str` because it's simpler" — that proposal is wrong because:
  - It re-introduces the empty-id failure mode the JMAP-6by7.2 refactor was
    designed to eliminate.
  - It puts validation back at the bottom of the call stack instead of at
    construction time.
  - It breaks the Email/parse vs Email/get composition where blob ids and
    email ids are distinguishable at the type level.

Defend by pointing to the comment trail in the test files (e.g.
email.rs:340-342) which document exactly which tests became impossible to
express under typed Id and were deleted.

The typed-Id refactor cost something — verbose call sites — but the
correctness payoff is large. Do not unwind.
title: Typed Id / State parameters across the method API — defend against weakening
